title: Add traceable customer-receipt allocations to Sales Orders
description: Add one canonical explicit allocation register between existing customer-receipt evidence and Sales Orders so users can record which orders a receipt document refers to without creating or executing a receipt. Reuse any equivalent authoritative persisted relationship already present in ERP-032 rather than creating a competing allocation model. Do not infer links, mark orders as settled, calculate a legal accounts-receivable balance, move funds, execute production SQL, deploy, or release.
acceptance_criteria: Users can maintain bounded allocation rows for an existing non-deleted customer-receipt evidence record, each referencing one existing non-cancelled Sales Order and recording an allocation amount plus bounded notes.

The implementation first audits and reuses any equivalent authoritative ERP-032 receipt-to-order relationship; the repository must end with one canonical persisted allocation model rather than two competing link schemas.

The server validates authoritative Customer and currency compatibility between the receipt evidence and every Sales Order; mismatches are rejected and are never converted, reassigned or matched by number, text, date or amount similarity.

The sum of active allocation rows cannot exceed the authoritative receipt-evidence amount, currency precision is enforced server-side, and duplicate active links to the same Sales Order within one receipt document are rejected.
Allocation rows preserve bounded receipt, Customer, Sales Order and currency snapshots so historical evidence remains identifiable when a referenced master record later becomes unavailable.
Users can void an incorrect allocation with a reason while preserving its original values and history; hard deletion, silent replacement and rewriting of previously voided evidence are not provided.
The workflow labels allocations as receipt-reference evidence rather than proof of bank settlement, legal discharge, accounts-receivable balance, customer statement or tax position.

Creating or voiding an allocation does not change the receipt document's execution state, Sales Order status, shipment progress, Customer credit state, inventory, invoices, commissions, expenses or tax records.
Existing receipt evidence and Sales Orders remain readable without allocation rows, and no request-time or production backfill is performed.
List and detail queries are bounded or paged and avoid per-row database queries; repository schema changes are idempotent and are validated only through permitted local or test-database paths.

Unit/integration tests cover full and partial allocation, multiple orders, Customer and currency mismatch, over-allocation, duplicate links, void history, legacy records, bounded queries and source-record non-mutation; safe validation passes and browser acceptance is recorded as deferred during development.

scenarios: Open an existing customer-receipt evidence record, allocate part of its amount to two compatible Sales Orders, and verify the traceable rows and remaining unallocated evidence without changing either order.

Attempt a Customer or currency mismatch and an over-allocation, verify they are rejected, then void a valid allocation and verify its history remains visible without presenting the receipt as settlement.

human_gate.reason: Repository allocation evidence and non-production test schema only. Real receipt execution, production database changes, irreversible finance operations, deployment and release remain behind mandatory human gates.
